# Dockerfile for lammps-reax
# Target Environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes
# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for broad compatibility and support.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# This allows running as root and forces TCP communication, which is common
# in container orchestrators where shared memory or high-speed interconnects
# are not available between pods.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,sm
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0

# Install build dependencies, runtime dependencies, and OpenMPI
# This is done in a single RUN layer to reduce image size.
# build-essential, cmake, git are for compiling LAMMPS.
# openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev are for MPI support.
# ca-certificates is for secure network communication (e.g., git clone).
# libgomp1 is a required runtime library for OpenMP.
# [FIX] python3 and python3-dev are required for the LAMMPS cmake build process.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    ca-certificates \
    libgomp1 \
    python3 \
    python3-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone the latest stable version of the LAMMPS source code
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git /opt/lammps

# Set the working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /opt/lammps/build

# Configure and build LAMMPS using CMake
# -D PKG_REAXFF=on: Enables the REAXFF package as requested for 'lammps-reax'.
# -D BUILD_MPI=yes: Explicitly enables MPI support.
# make -j$(nproc): Compiles the code using all available CPU cores.
RUN cmake -D PKG_REAXFF=on -D BUILD_MPI=yes ../cmake && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled LAMMPS executable to a location on the system's PATH
# This makes 'lmp' directly available to users and scripts.
RUN cp /opt/lammps/build/lmp /usr/local/bin/

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the example files for the HNS simulation into the working directory
RUN cp /opt/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* .

# Clean up build dependencies and source code to reduce the final image size.
# This is a crucial step for a production-ready image.
# [FIX] Purge python3 and python3-dev as they are only build dependencies.
RUN apt-get purge -y --auto-remove \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    python3 \
    python3-dev \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /opt/lammps && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a default command to start an interactive shell
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
#
# MiniCluster YAML manifest for a LAMMPS ReaxFF experiment on Kubernetes.
# This manifest is designed for the Flux Operator (v1alpha2) to run a single-node,
# multi-task HPC job in an AWS CPU environment.
#
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster experiment.
  name: lammps-reax-aws-cpu
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as per instructions.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster StatefulSet. Set to 1 for a single-node run.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run across the MiniCluster.
  # Since size is 1, all 4 tasks will run on the single pod.
  tasks: 4

  # Keep pods and services after the job is complete for debugging and log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Fail on any error, do not continue. This ensures a robust, production-like behavior.
    strict: true

  # Defines the container that will run the HPC application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command is executed by the Flux scheduler within the container.
      # The Flux Operator will prepend 'flux run -n <tasks> ...' to this command.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # When 'launcher' is false, this container is part of the Flux instance and runs the application.
      launcher: false
      # No resource limits or requests are set, allowing the pod to be 'Burstable'
      # and utilize all available node resources, which is typical for HPC batch jobs.

updates.reason: The initial 4-task run was a misconfigured baseline. This attempt scales up to a 64-core HPC instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) and configures the LAMMPS process grid to match the core count, which is expected to significantly reduce wall time.

The previous run on a 64-core ARM instance achieved a 5-second wall time. This attempt will test the highest-core-count x86 instance (c7a.12xlarge, 48 AMD cores) to compare architectural performance. The task count and processor grid are adjusted to fully utilize the new instance.

Achieved a wall time of 5 seconds on both a 64-core ARM instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) and a 48-core AMD instance (c7a.12xlarge). This indicates the performance has plateaued, and further increases in core count are unlikely to yield significant improvements due to scaling limits or communication overhead. The current 5-second result is considered optimized.

      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge
